column1: # AQL Language Specification: Arithmetic (add sub mul div mod pow)
# The binary math words follow the kernel's ONE convention: the handler
# computes `args[1] OP args[0]`, so the SWAP form `a op b` reads naturally
# (`10 sub 3 = 7`, `20 div 4 = 5`, `2 pow 10 = 1024`) while the pure
# forward form `op a b` computes `b OP a` (`sub 10 3 = 3-10 = -7`). add and
# mul are commutative so both forms agree. Integer/Integer stays Integer
# (integer division truncates); any Float operand promotes to Float.
# §2  sub / div / mod / pow — non-commutative (handler computes b OP a)
# §3  add concatenates as String only when AT LEAST ONE operand is a
#     String; the other Scalar coerces (b ++ a, mirroring b OP a). Two
#     non-String scalars match neither overload → type error (WAT §G).

column3: Integer + String → String concat 'x'++'1' (one operand is a String)
String + String concatenates in b++a order
Boolean + String → the String operand admits concat, Boolean coerces
String + Float coerces the Float to its string form
Boolean + Integer: neither is a String → no concat, type error
two Booleans: neither is a String → type error (was silently 'falsetrue')
Integer and Float of equal magnitude compare equal
integer division by zero (no integer infinity)
Float 0/0 is IEEE-754 NaN, not an error
`mod 7 0` = 0 mod 7 = 0 (divisor is the swapped operand, no error)
add is binary: the third value is left on the stack

column1: # §6  integer overflow — a uniform error, never a silent wrap or Float

column3: one below maxint is still in range — no error
product exceeds int64 (was a silent two's-complement wrap)
2^63 overflows (was a silent wrap to minint)
2^62 is the largest in-range power of two — no error
a large but in-range product is unaffected
a Float operand opts out of the integer check (IEEE-754 result)
